Theory & Math

Follow the equations that connect pressure, elevation, and wall friction to the computed network flows.

View equations ↓
SymbolsEquationsSolver methodValidationReferences

Symbols and units

The workspace models steady flow of a single, incompressible Newtonian liquid through full, circular pipes. All elevations use the same datum. Plan coordinates arrange the drawing. The 3D view uses the physical elevation z.

SymbolMeaningUnit
H, z, hfPiezometric head, physical elevation, friction head-loss magnitudem
pg, ρ, g, μGauge pressure, density, gravitational acceleration, dynamic viscosityPa, kg/m³, m/s², Pa·s
L, D, ε, APipe length, inside diameter, absolute roughness, cross-sectional aream, m, m, m²
Q, v, SSigned pipe flow, signed mean velocity, signed external injection at a nodem³/s, m/s, m³/s
Re, fFReynolds number, Fanning friction factorDimensionless

Governing equations

Boundary conditions and continuity

H = z + pg/(ρg)
Σ Qout − Σ Qin = S

A pressure boundary fixes the head through elevation and gauge pressure. The workspace converts pressure entered in kPa to Pa. A flow boundary enters a positive magnitude and uses node type to set the sign of S. Junctions have S = 0. Each connected component requires a pressure reference.

Pipe resistance and sign convention

A = πD²/4   ·   v = Q/A   ·   Re = ρ|v|D/μ
Ha − Hb = 4fF (L/D) v|v|/(2g)

Positive flow follows the entered direction from endpoint a to b. A negative result reverses the arrows. The results table reports the head-loss magnitude hf. The model uses g = 9.80665 m/s² and a fixed roughness of 0.000015 m as a model input.

Fanning friction factor

For flowing pipes at Re below 100, the implementation uses the laminar limit fF = 16/Re. Otherwise it evaluates Churchill’s correlation, with dimensionless intermediate quantities C and B. The Darcy factor is 4fF.

C = [−2.457 ln((7/Re)0.9 + 0.27ε/D)]16
B = (37530/Re)16
fF = 2[(8/Re)12 + (C + B)−3/2]1/12

At zero flow the friction loss is zero and the factor is undefined. See Churchill’s original paper.

Solver method and course connections

Bisection determines each signed flow for a trial head drop. Damped Newton iteration adjusts the unknown heads until the largest absolute continuity residual is below 10−10 m³/s. The live model includes elevation and wall friction. Pump curves, fitting losses, valves, and tank-filling dynamics belong outside this workspace’s calculation scope.

Course topicWhere to see it
Continuity and energy balance (Weeks 10–11)Compare prescribed boundaries with solved junction heads and the flow residual.
Fanning friction and laminar flow (HW4)Compare Reynolds numbers and review the Hagen–Poiseuille validation case.
Diameter selection (Week 12 and HW5)Change one diameter, then compare the resulting pressure, flow, and velocity in Economics.

Validation checks

Run the six built-in cases against the same solver used by the network workspace. Each check reports the expected value, computed value, and tolerance.

Diameter selection

At a given flow, a larger pipe reduces velocity and friction losses. In the network, changing a diameter can also change the operating point, so compare the new flow, velocity, and pressure after each edit. Annual cost calculations are pending the HW5 cost inputs. [R2]

Team and AI workflow

The team used AI to help build and evaluate a fluid mechanics simulator. The students defined the model scope, tested the resulting calculations, and compared two approaches to the same network problem.

  • Ian SniderProject lead, initial refinery build with Muse, and assistant presenter
  • Drew CorbittSecond-model comparison assignment and lead presenter
  • Perry MeredithSlide deck and video support
  • Zac NeikampStandalone piping simulator, video production, and narration

Implementation comparison

Design choiceEarlier refinery buildZac’s live workspace
Model scopeFixed-head networks with pump-assisted transfer, pipe and fitting losses, and over-the-top fill calculationsPassive networks with wall friction, physical elevation, and pressure or flow boundaries
InteractionEditable tables and a generated schematicSynchronized tables and canvas, with 2D plan and 3D elevation views
VerificationPython reference and JavaScript cross-checkSix built-in browser checks for balances, boundaries, and limiting cases

Open the live validation checks

Project decisions

  • Use Zac’s workspace as the live simulator. Its pressure and flow boundary controls and physical elevation views define the calculation scope.
  • Use the Fanning convention throughout. The equations, worked calculation, and pipe results use the same friction factor.
  • Present velocity screening as a design check. The Economics tab reads the live pipe velocities. Annual cost requires a separate model and inputs.

The team’s detailed comparison of prompts, model versions, and final conclusions is pending.
